subject: [Novapay] Model shortlist & workload snapshot for onboarding
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Emilia Torres <emilia.torres@novapay.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Novapay — initial workload snapshot & shortlist (see attachments)

Hi Emilia / Carlos,

Thanks again for running through the pilot metrics yesterday. As discussed, I put together a compact snapshot to align on model candidates and expected token load during the 90-day ramp. Attached: a token-profile workbook (novapay_token_profile_v1.xlsx) and a one-pager with the shortlist rationale (model_shortlist_rationale.pdf).

High-level summary:
- Peak concurrent user flows: ~140 reqs/min during settlement batch window (13:00–14:30 UTC).
- Median prompt length ~220 tokens (including metadata), expected response ~160–220 tokens depending on fallback depth.
- Estimated steady-state daily tokens (conservative): 32M; ramp peak-day forecast: 78M.

Model shortlist (recommended priority):
1) redwood-llama-70b-q4f (cost/latency balance; good with 8k context)
2) community-mistral-32k (for longer-context flows, useful for full-wallet histories)
3) redwood-3b-qual (low-cost fallback for high-volume non-critical paths)

Questions for you before we lock the implementation plan:
- Are there any additional verbose system prompts we need to include in the prefix sizing (e.g., legal disclaimers appended to each prompt)?
- Do you expect more multi-turn sessions per request than indicated in the workbook?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the prefix requirements by EOD Tuesday (21 Dec).
- We finalize the model window and throughput assumptions and hand to Eng for Dedicated sizing (Marissa will take point).

Thanks — I left some inline notes on the spreadsheet where I adjusted sample rates.

Best,
Tessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: novapay_token_profile_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 420KB), model_shortlist_rationale.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@novapay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Emilia Torres <emilia.torres@novapay.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Novapay — initial workload snapshot & shortlist (see attachments)

Thanks, Tessa — this looks very helpful. Quick clarifications: 

1) Prefix requirements: legal wants a short safety disclaimer added to any message that touches PII; it will add ~40 tokens to the prompt. We'll loop in compliance if you need specific wording but for sizing please assume +40 tokens per relevant request.

2) Multi-turn sessions: for support chat flows, we see an average of 2.3 turns per user (some walk-through flows hit 5+ turns). For automated reconciliation prompts it's usually single-turn. For the ramp plan, please use 2.5 turns on customer-facing chat paths.

I'll review the spreadsheet and call out any adjustments by EOD. Also, curious on the expected latency for the shortlisted models at 8k vs 32k context — can you summarize that for Marissa/Eng?

—Carlos
Head of Integrations, Novapay

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Emilia Torres <emilia.torres@novapay.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@novapay.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T10:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Novapay — initial workload snapshot & shortlist (see attachments)

Marissa / Ben — looping you in for implementation sizing and latency tradeoffs.

Carlos — thanks for the clarifications. I've updated the workbook with +40 tokens to any PII-touching path and bumped the multi-turn multiplier to 2.5 for customer chat. The workbook now shows:
- Conservative day: 34.7M tokens/day (includes +40 token prefix on 48% of traffic).
- Ramp peak-day: 81.9M tokens/day.
- Hourly peak (settlement window): ~6.2M tokens/hour.

Model-latency summary (very rough 95th pct estimates, single-request end-to-end generation time):
- redwood-llama-70b-q4f (8k): 420–520 ms
- redwood-llama-70b-q4f (32k): 700–950 ms
- community-mistral-32k: 850–1,100 ms (32k context optimized)
- redwood-3b-qual: 120–190 ms (good fallback for non-blocking paths)

Proposed implementation handoff items for Eng (Marissa):
1) Dedicated capacity baseline: 3 x A100s reserved for 70b traffic, autoscale policy to add 2 nodes at 70% sustained CPU/GPU; burst pool for peak settlement window.
2) Route policy: priority-route to 70b for critical flows; fallback to 3b for non-critical and retry on degradation.
3) Cache policy: KV prefix caching for repeat account histories; expect 18–24% token savings in typical flows.

I've attached an updated spreadsheet copy (novapay_token_profile_v1.xlsx) with the numbers and a short change log. Can you confirm Marissa that the A100 baseline is something Eng is comfortable sizing for Dedicated, or should we tweak to mixed-instance (A100 + H100) planning?

I'll schedule a 30-min handoff call for Mon 12/23 10:00 PST unless you prefer Wed.

Thanks,
Tessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: novapay_token_profile_v1.xlsx (updated, 460KB)
